title: CRPS-stacked ensemble weights — crps_weights
text: R wrapper mirrors `lopensemble::crps_weights`. Optimises weights softmax space empirical mixture-CRPS objective Dirichlet log-prior penalty.

title: CRPS-stacked ensemble weights — crps_weights
text: training data frame columns `model_id`, `output_type` (must `"sample"`), `output_type_id`, `value`, plus task-id columns. observations data frame task-id columns plus `observed`. task_id_cols Character vector task-id columns. dirichlet_alpha Concentration Dirichlet log-prior penalty. Default 1.001 matches `lopensemble`.

title: CRPS-stacked ensemble weights — crps_weights
text: data frame columns `model_id` `weight`.

title: CRPS-stacked ensemble weights — crps_weights
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ set.seed(1) taus_per_task <- 100 n_task <- 30 y <- rnorm(n_task)  make_samples <- function(model_id, sampler) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_task), function(t) data.frame(     model_id = model_id, output_type = "sample",     output_type_id = seq_len(taus_per_task),     t = t, value = sampler(y[t]),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ))) } train <- rbind(   make_samples("m_good",  function(yt) yt + rnorm(taus_per_task, sd = 0.4)),   make_samples("m_noisy", function(yt) rnorm(taus_per_task, sd = 3)) ) obs <- data.frame(t = seq_len(n_task), observed = y) crps_weights(train, obs, task_id_cols = "t") } # }

title: Linear opinion pool — linear_pool
text: R wrapper mirrors `hubEnsembles::linear_pool`. Routes `output_type` `model_out_tbl`: samples pooled, CDFs averaged, quantile inputs go CDF reconstruction (PCHIP + normal tails).

title: Linear opinion pool — linear_pool
text: model_out_tbl data frame columns `model_id`, `output_type`, `output_type_id`, `value`, plus task-id columns. weights Optional data frame columns `model_id` `weight`. n_samples Pooled-sample size sampling/quantile paths. task_id_cols Character vector task-id columns.

title: Linear opinion pool — linear_pool
text: data frame shape, `model_id = "hub-ensemble"`.

title: Linear opinion pool — linear_pool
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Quantile-input path: each model contributes a 5-quantile forecast; the # linear pool reconstructs each CDF, samples, then re-extracts quantiles. df <- expand.grid(   model_id       = c("m1", "m2"),   output_type_id = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9),   location       = "A",   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) df$output_type <- "quantile" df$value <- qnorm(df$output_type_id,                   mean = ifelse(df$model_id == "m1", 0, 2),                   sd   = 1) linear_pool(df, n_samples = 5000, task_id_cols = "location") } # }

title: Quantile Regression Averaging — qra
text: R wrapper mirrors `qrensemble::qra`. Fits quantile regression training forecasts applies fitted weights target forecasts.

title: Quantile Regression Averaging — qra
code: qra(   training,   target,   observations,   task_id_cols,   per_quantile_weights = FALSE,   intercept = FALSE,   enforce_normalisation = TRUE,   noncross = TRUE,   group = character(0) )

title: Quantile Regression Averaging — qra
text: training data frame columns `model_id`, `output_type` (must `"quantile"`), `output_type_id`, `value`, plus task-id columns. target data frame shape — forecasts combine using fitted weights. observations data frame task-id columns plus `observed`. task_id_cols Character vector task-id columns. per_quantile_weights TRUE, fit separate weights per quantile. intercept Include intercept term regression. enforce_normalisation Constrain weights lie simplex. noncross Add cross-quantile monotonicity constraints (used `per_quantile_weights = TRUE`). group Character vector task dimensions fit separate regressions.

title: Quantile Regression Averaging — qra
text: data frame fitted predictions `target`.

title: Quantile Regression Averaging — qra
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # 50 training points, 1 holdout, 2 component models, 5 quantile levels. set.seed(1) taus <- c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9) n <- 50 y <- rnorm(n + 1) make_rows <- function(model_id, predictions) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(taus, function(q) data.frame(     model_id = model_id, output_type = "quantile",     output_type_id = q, t = seq_along(predictions),     value = predictions + qnorm(q),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ))) } rows <- rbind(   make_rows("m_good",  y + 0.3 * rnorm(n + 1)),   make_rows("m_noisy", 2 * rnorm(n + 1)) ) train  <- rows[rows$t <= n,  ] target <- rows[rows$t == n + 1, ] obs <- data.frame(t = seq_len(n), observed = y[seq_len(n)])  qra(training = train, target = target, observations = obs,     task_id_cols = "t", enforce_normalisation = TRUE,     intercept = FALSE, noncross = TRUE) } # }
